hook.title: I taught an AI to drive

lines.say: I made a rally game, and taught an AI to drive in it.
This is its very first try.
And this is the same AI, eighty minutes later.
So how does it work? First, it never sees the screen.
Ten times a second, it gets forty-six numbers.
Nine rays measure how far away the edge of the road is.
Fourteen points show where the road goes next.
The rest is its speed, how much it slides, and what it's pressing.
A small neural network turns those numbers into a move: steer, throttle, brake, or handbrake.
At first, it's just guessing.
Nobody tells it how to drive. It only gets a score.
Plus one for every twenty meters of road.
Minus three when it crashes or leaves the road.
After every round, the moves that scored more become a bit more likely, and the ones that scored less, less likely.
Try, score, adjust, repeat. That's reinforcement learning.
Sixty-four cars practice at once, on one Mac.
Eighty minutes of this is almost a week of driving.
After three minutes, most of them reach this corner, and fly off.
After half an hour, most of them make it round.
After eighty minutes, forty-five of sixty-four finish the whole stage.
Then the real test: a road it has never seen.
It never practised here, and still, sixty-one of sixty-four make it to the finish.
It's in my game now. Press I, and it drives for you. Or race its old generations as ghosts.
